label: H.R. 9203

latest_action.text: Placed on the Union Calendar, Calendar No. 700.

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: H.R. 9203, the Student Protection and University Accountability Act, requires colleges and universities that participate in federal student aid programs to establish specific processes for investigating complaints related to Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964. It sets deadlines for schools to respond to complaints, requires them to keep records, mandates public posting of federal civil rights awareness materials, and penalizes schools that fail to comply for two consecutive years by making them ineligible for federal student aid. Additionally, the bill requires the Department of Education's Office for Civil Rights to give bimonthly briefings and reports to Congress and restricts how it dismisses or delays certain complaints.

affected_groups.effect: Must establish and publicize specific Title VI investigative procedures, designate coordinators, maintain detailed records, display federal awareness materials, submit annual compliance attestations, and risk losing federal student aid eligibility if noncompliant for two consecutive years.

Receive wider distribution of civil rights complaint procedures, strict 30-day notification timelines regarding complaints and investigation outcomes, and contact information for reporting violations to the school and the Department of Education.
Must provide bimonthly briefings and written reports to designated congressional committees and change internal procedures regarding the dismissal and delay of complaints.
affected_groups.group: Department of Education Office for Civil Rights

key_provisions: Requires institutions of higher education to create and widely distribute clear procedures for investigating Title VI civil rights complaints.
Mandates that schools designate at least one Title VI coordinator and maintain detailed record-keeping systems for all complaints, outcomes, and remedial actions.
Requires schools to notify complainants within 30 days of receiving a complaint whether an investigation has been opened, and within 30 days of an outcome being reached.
Requires schools to publicly display and publish Department of Education civil rights public awareness campaign materials on campus and online.
Penalizes schools that fail to comply with these requirements for two consecutive award years by making them ineligible for federal student aid for at least two subsequent award years.

Requires the Department of Education's Office for Civil Rights to provide bimonthly congressional briefings and written reports regarding Title VI complaints, methods of addressing them, and investigation lengths.

Prohibits the Office for Civil Rights from closing, dismissing, or delaying a TitleVI complaint simply because another complaint involving the same allegations was filed elsewhere by the complainant or another individual, with narrow exceptions.
missing_information: The precise number of institutions expected to fail compliance or lose federal student aid.
The exact financial impact or administrative cost on colleges and universities to implement these record-keeping and notification systems.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 9203, the Student Protection and University Accountability Act, requires colleges and universities that participate in federal student aid programs to establish specific processes for investigating complaints related to Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964. It sets deadlines for schools to respond to complaints, requires them to keep records, mandates public posting of federal civil rights awareness materials, and penalizes schools that fail to comply for two consecutive years by making them ineligible for federal student aid. Additionally, the bill requires the Department of Education's Office for Civil Rights to give bimonthly briefings and reports to Congress and restricts how it dismisses or delays certain complaints.
summary_detail.significance: The bill increases federal oversight of how colleges and universities handle discrimination complaints based on race, color, or national origin under Title VI. It establishes mandatory institutional compliance rules tied to federal student aid eligibility and alters how federal civil rights offices process and report complaints to Congress.
